negative_reviews.author: morgan lee
negative_reviews.text:
My third time visiting since opening and it was a really poor experience, I had brought my niece (11 and autistic) out for some lunch as we had signed up to the app and received vouchers for a £5 ramen she was so excited, we went to oseyo opposite the restaurant and bought some snacks and drink before going to grab a table, once we were sat it took a while for someone to take our order, when the food arrived we only received one order, the server only put one meal on the tab so i had waited over 30 minutes for my meal and my niece was already half way through her food.
We were almost finished and ready to ask for the bill, when the White female manager noticed our drinks we had bought from the shop placed next to my bag where my niece was sitting, she asked us to put them away which i agreed to and told my niece to try and fit them into the bag she couldn’t hear me due to the loud atmosphere and before i could repeat myself the manager had took it upon herself to tell my niece to put them away but she adopted a different tone when speaking to my niece which i didn’t appreciate as i had already agreed to put them away, she explained that the reason for them needing to be put away was due to allergies which as someone who works in the hospitality/ food industry and is fully aware of Natasha’s law that is not something i was confused by the logic, I also visited two weeks before and had no issue with bringing my own drink so it must be something they have recently implemented. The interaction left me very uncomfortable so i asked for the bill and when it came to paying it had to be split which wasn’t an issue but after leaving and checking my bank statement I had noticed i was charger £5.50 rather than £5 despite using the £5 voucher, I don’t know what the extra charges were for as the receipt i received was the original one with the price before the vouchers had been applied. Overall a lot went wrong and i feel there is a lot to be improved, especially in terms of service and ordering processes.

negative_reviews.author: Saraiba Hassan
negative_reviews.text: Horrible Food, absolutely not worth the money! The squid tempura was chewy and flavourless. Had the steak ramen and it was chewy and inedible had to send it back. Not worth the money!

negative_reviews.author: Hasib Khan
negative_reviews.text: Customer service was mid. They have us well done steak ramen, extremely cheewy. Food is not the best.

negative_reviews.author: Heavenly Magogo
negative_reviews.text: This place has good food however the service and communication skills is VERY disappointing.when it came to communicating with us to why we got kicked out the brown male staff member was cussing under his breath about his job after each customer .Mind you they did not clarify why we got kicked out coming to the conclusion it’s because we were being too loud but there was music louder than our voices . as well there was a middle age woman who was stereotypical towards us how being a teenagers and lied about warning us about being loud. This shows the poor attitude of staff to younger people who are trying to enjoy their friends company and the food.

negative_reviews.author: Blessing Magogo
negative_reviews.text:
Please be aware if you are a teenager they will be on to you.They have preconceptions about us teens especially this one middle aged white lady who seems to have an agressive attitude ,kicked me and my friends out (as if we weren’t going to leave already) for simply having fun and enjoying the food like any other customer minding our business because supposedly we are not allowed to laugh because we was making noise ? Mind you there was full load music going on.

One of her employees (brown boy with black hair perhaps in 20s)had a big attitude problem as he kept whispering under his breath cuss words and complaining about people having an attitude yet he’s the one with it..like are you slow. on about some “ sorry is there something funny” mind you the conversation had nothing to do with him.And when he saw my friend he was like “ oh those girls again” like respectfully shut up and I don’t know why he’s scared of teens .

Then, when we called the shop again to know why we had to leave (after they kicked us out) the women said she warned us about being loud and how if we do that again we will leave yet she NEVER said that to our face at all and then she proceeded to say “ if u want to be stupid we have cameras” (we recorded the conversation) well nah obviously you have them and you will see how she didn’t interact with us until we had to pay by accusing us we had added other foods because previous teens brought lots of food and lied about having one bowl ..like respectfully u shouldn’t be making assumptions/comparing us to pervious situations .

Over all , the food was good .However, when it comes to customer service and professionalism it is very disappointing and embarrassing how staff treat teenagers by  calling us stupid when she’s the  one who stupidly doesn’t know how to respond respectfully to the question ”why did you kick us out?”

seems like some adults need to go back and learn basic communication skills. And re think about applying to work in a social environment because the male staff member is clearly fed up with their job yet is still there. Then the women , Acting like showing the cameras will do something. like are you dumb ? of course we know what we did because we was there

negative_reviews.author: Bogdan Artemov
negative_reviews.text: absolutely horrible service! Had plastic in my food and took forever to get a new dish... guy behind me had the same issue! also had lipstick on my glass and asked for a replacement but never got one despite asking for it again!! clearly not fresh ingredients and absolutely unacceptable service!! i wont be coming back anytime soon

negative_reviews.author: Olivia Allen
negative_reviews.text: Safe to say disappointed doesn’t even begin to cover, after having a lovely time in the Nottingham branch this place does a disservice to the brand. You’ve got team members who are miserable clearly not being managed which is strange due to the amount on. It is clear as anything that servers haven’t learnt the menu, let alone how to communicate to the customers. Really disappointed came away with such a distaste. You’ve lost some loyal customers .

negative_reviews.author: San Dee (Sandee)
negative_reviews.text:
We visited on a Thursday evening, it wasn't too busy which was nice.
The food was good, we had a steak ramen, a chicken yakisoba and Tokyo rolls.
It was generally good, I wouldn't rush to go there again.
We also had a lychee lemonade with bubble tea. It tasted really nice but the portion was tiny, again for the price. Should have been a full cup but it was tiny.
It let itself down with the price, it was really expensive for what you get.
Other than that nice location, good staff.

negative_reviews.author: Crow
negative_reviews.text:
The food here was ok. I had a bowl of ramen, which was alright and my friends had chicken katsu curry and sushi. Apparently the sushi was very good, but I feel like the ramen was mediocre - lots of other places do much better ramen for cheaper.
They have a different kitchen for their sushi so if you're in a group ordering a mix of sushi and hot mains, be aware that it could take longer for one to arrive. We waited for quite a long time before my friend was served the sushi she ordered.
The atmosphere was also very nice

negative_reviews.author: Trish Vu
negative_reviews.text: I was appalled with the level of customer service there was. Not only we were giving our drinks AFTER our food was served and eaten, we saw the table next to us being seated down after us and given their drinks before us. There was an incident where I asked for the bill by I assumed was the manager on duty, and she said that there was a delay as they had to print out 8 bills and the receipt machine was having problems, we waited roughly 20-25 minutes without any communications while the blonde lady looked at us a lot, we then saw the table next to us asking for the bill and immediately got their receipt even though we waited for some times. I told the other waiter that we have been waited for ages and I told the lady we needed the bill and he said “oh” without any apologies on her behalf which makes us believe they did not really care about our time.

negative_reviews.author: Nina
negative_reviews.text:
Hells ramen was not spicy. So they charge for extra chilli sauce!
They were half empty and we had ordered too much food for a table of 2 to fit properly. But they were too inflexible to move us.
So the food was ok. Service could be better and if the spicy ramen isn't hot enough they shouldn't be charging for more chilli.

negative_reviews.author: Natalie Chatterton
negative_reviews.text: Delicious food, lots to choose from, but the resturant was soo crowded and loud, it was difficult to hear anyone talking.

issues: Spencer Copley has taken over as GM and presented at the England KPI meeting, as Birmingham has now joined Inka Cheung's region.
Covers were 2,498, up 23 (0.92%) week on week and consistent over recent weeks.
Spend per head fell to £22.92, down £0.52 (2.21%), with over 300 £5 ramens redeemed since Thursday.
Sales were £59,515.49, down £30.02 (0.05%) week on week and £6,515.49 (12.29%) ahead of target.
Labour was 24.84%, with two weekdays above 30%; the aim is below 23% next week by cutting hours and lengthening breaks.
Front of house needs to cut more labour than the kitchen, and Roger needs more guidance on cutting hours.
At the BOH meeting the agreed rota plan is to reduce weekday hours and move cover to weekend peaks; Srawut's review found the kitchen needs to save about £18 a day and FOH about £200 a day.
Sophie cautioned that labour cuts must not compromise food quality, complaints or allergy safety at a new site, and FOH needs time to train new staff after several leavers before hours are cut.
Variance was about £150 to £160 after last week's figure of around £1,400 was traced to an ordering input error.
Food cost looked high but was offset by almost £10,000 of promotion and discount losses; adjusted, it is around 21%, which is very good.
Five or six items, mostly bar stock, ran out on Sunday, so more alcohol and wet products are being ordered.
The Google rating dropped to 4.7 after a bad week, including two 1 star reviews believed to be from a former staff member and their partner; about 166 five star reviews are needed to get back to 4.8.
Managers will do check-backs on every table, fix problems immediately and may give out free edamame to recover reviews.
Communication from management is a stated area for improvement.
Sunday evening delivery was very busy, with three passive orders and prep time up slightly because of large orders.
Inaccurate delivery orders were zero for the first time, and the delivery overall rating was 4.3, below where the site wants it.
Birmingham set up a WhatsApp group where FOH staff post delivery order photos straight away to defend disputes, which Inka praised as a practice for other sites.
Two new bartenders and a new front of house team member have started, and a sushi chef starts in about two weeks.
The new full time sushi starter begins on 20/10 after a trial and closing observation on 18/10.
Compliance dropped to 87% from 100% the week before, so the closing manager will now double check all closing duties.
Birmingham does not yet run the lunch menu, which every other England site has.
Birmingham's table toppers still carry the Trip material and need to match the three item standard.
No audit was done this week.
Ticket delays came from the ramen section being very busy while the 'dump' (as transcribed) and fry section was slow, so a kitchen supervisor will be stationed there.
Plastic pieces were found in ramen broth that do not match the broth bags or noodle packaging, and an extra straining step for new broth batches was agreed.
Sophie flagged tempura and squid in review photos as flavourless and poorly prepared, and squid had been seen pre-cooked and served cold without reheating, with small, oily portions.
A delayed sushi order on Friday drew a negative review, put down to high volume and limited staffing on the section.
Front of house staff often do not know the dishes they serve, for example mistaking pink ginger for salmon, and food has gone to the wrong tables.
A chef referred by Roger, who previously turned Birmingham down, is to be approached again.
Region-wide (England): the £5 ramen offer is now limited to one per person through a backend change, announced by Amy Tang at the 06/10 KPI meeting.

Region-wide (England): the Mapal compliance app (transcribed as 'Maple') must be installed on site laptops and iPads, with photos sent to the management chat; front of house staff may no longer use personal phones for compliance on shift, while kitchen staff may use their own phones.

Region-wide (England): table toppers must carry exactly one drink menu, one XOXO drink and one ramen loyalty card, and marketing material requests go to the England group chat for Amy Tang to forward to marketing.

Region-wide (England): at the 06/10 BOH meeting Sophie asked sites to top up stock through the promotions rather than hold back for food cost limits, to monitor dashboard stock levels, and to stop borrowing stock between branches.
